sourceText: Arts [ARTS] CHEM 105 [PSCI] ENGLISH 101 [WRTG] Humanities [HUM] MATH 106 The minimum math requirement is MATH 140. Students who place into MATH 140 or higher are not required to take MATH 106 or 108 but must take an additional 5 credits of electives. MATH 171 may be substituted for MATH 140. Students who place into MATH 140 should take it during their first year, and may delay one of the UCORE courses [ARTS], [HUM], or [SSCI]. Social Sciences [SSCI] CHEM 220 CHEM 222 Diversity [DIVR] MATH 140 [QUAN] The minimum math requirement is MATH 140. Students who place into MATH 140 or higher are not required to take MATH 106 or 108 but must take an additional 5 credits of electives. MATH 171 may be substituted for MATH 140. Students who place into MATH 140 should take it during their first year, and may delay one of the UCORE courses [ARTS], [HUM], or [SSCI]. PHYSICS 101 PHYSICS 201/211 and 202/212 may be substituted for PHYSICS 101/111 and 102/112. PHYSICS 111 PHYSICS 201/211 and 202/212 may be substituted for PHYSICS 101/111 and 102/112. BIOLOGY 106 or 107 CHEM 301 PHYSICS 102 PHYSICS 201/211 and 202/212 may be substituted for PHYSICS 101/111 and 102/112. PHYSICS 112 PHYSICS 201/211 and 202/212 may be substituted for PHYSICS 101/111 and 102/112. Electives At least 11 credits in addition to those specified must be at the 300-400-level, for a total of at least 40 upper division credits. Complete Writing Portfolio CHEM 338 or 331 CHEM 331 has prerequisites of PHYSICS 202 or 206, and MATH 273, each with a C or better. CHEM 345 CHEM 398 STAT 212 CHEM 348 CHEM 370 or MBIOS 303 ENGLISH 402 [WRTG] [M] Equity and Justice [EQJS] Advanced Chemistry Electives Advanced Chemistry Electives (minimum 5 credits): Approved courses include CHEM 347, 425, 426, 490, 499 (maximum 2 credits), any 500-level CHEM course, or STAT 412. Other electives may be used with permission. Foreign Language, if needed, or Electives The Foreign Language requirement is that of the College of Arts and Sciences and may be fulfilled with two years of a foreign language in high school. Students are encouraged to pursue a minor while fulfilling the electives requirement. At least 11 credits in addition to those specified must be at the 300-400-level, for a total of at least 40 upper division credits. CHEM 485 [CAPS] [M] Exit Interview Admission to the Major Requirements A student may be admitted as a Chemistry major upon declaring their intent to the department. To maintain good standing in the major, students must complete CHEM 105 and 106 (or 116) and MATH 171, each with a grade of C or better, by the time they earn 30 credits. Students must also have a grade of C or better in all Chemistry courses. Failure to do so may result in the student being released from the major.
